ApiErrorResponseSchema.c2a0d71.description:

It mirrors ``build_error_response()`` in ``app/utils/flask_error_handlers.py``;
change both together. Use it to document error responses in ``@api.validate``,
for example ``HTTP_502=ApiErrorResponseSchema`` on an endpoint that calls an

get.description:
Exchanges authorization code for tokens and sets access token cookie.

Query Parameters:     code: Authorization code from OIDC provider     state: CSRF token from OIDC provider

Returns:     302: Redirect to original redirect URL with access token cookie set     400: Invalid or missing callback parameters     401: Token exchange failed
get.summary: Handle OIDC callback after user authorization.

get.description:
Generates authorization URL and redirects to OIDC provider. PKCE state is encrypted into the OAuth state parameter. The ``redirect_uri`` is the callback on the origin the request came in on, so the app signs in on every hostname it is served on (each one registered at the IdP).

Query Parameters:     redirect: Path to redirect to after successful login (required)

Returns:     302: Redirect to OIDC provider authorization endpoint     400: Missing or invalid redirect parameter
get.summary: Initiate OIDC login flow with PKCE.

get.description:
Clears access token cookie and redirects to OIDC provider's logout endpoint to terminate the session at the IdP level.

Query Parameters:     redirect: Path to redirect to after logout (default: /)

Returns:     302: Redirect to OIDC logout endpoint (or direct redirect if OIDC disabled)     400: Invalid redirect parameter

This endpoint is @public, so the request hook resolves the caller (refreshing an expired access token) without answering 401 itself, and the handler answers 401 when no one is signed in. A caller with none of the app's roles gets 403 from the hook. With OIDC disabled, the caller is the local admin.

Returns:     200: User information     401: No valid token provided or token invalid     403: User authenticated but has none of the app's roles

post.summary: FR-9, FR-20: a push to the store's main queues a pull and reindex; the relay gives each receiver four seconds, so nothing is pulled before the answer.
FR-27: a prompt run's outcome. The held run's releases the hold and starts the actioner again as its ending asks, off the request; a delivery for any other run is ignored.

FR-20, FR-21: an event naming an issue that is some observation's card queues a board sync of it; every other event is ignored without a call to YouTrack. The Webhook Triggers app waits for each answer, so nothing is read or written before it, and it sends the delivery before YouTrack commits the change, so the read waits `settle` seconds.

post.description:
This endpoint receives callbacks from the SSE Gateway when clients connect or disconnect. It extracts the request_id from the callback URL and calls SSEConnectionManager, which then notifies observers.

A connect is accepted only for a caller the API would serve, and is refused before it is registered, so a refused stream never receives an event and never counts in the connection metrics. The gateway turns a refusal into an in-stream ``rejected`` event and ends the stream.

Returns:     200 with an empty object on success

Raises:     AuthenticationException: 401, the callback secret fails (production         only), or the forwarded token is missing or invalid     AuthorizationException: 403, the caller holds none of the app's roles         (or lacks the read role, where one is set)     ValidationException: 400, the body is not a JSON object, the action         is unknown, or the request_id is missing or malformed     pydantic.ValidationError: 400, the payload is not a valid callback
post.summary: Handle SSE Gateway connect/disconnect callbacks.
